decision: English adverbs need no separate treatment by adverb class for nonpermutability: sentence, VP and verb adverbs already sit in different positions. Whether a class needs its own qualification rule was left to a new issue if a case arises.
No new double-object position for English: v:obj-R and v:rec already cover the double-object and dative alternation.

Diagnostic classes are defined in their own schema file (diagnostic_classes.yaml), separate from the codebook of criteria; each language lists the classes and constructions it uses in its own diagnostics file.
Araona's ciscategorial diagnostics add a PRED-combines criterion for predicative elements (English needs only V-combines); a position qualifies only if every *-combines criterion is n.

The Elements column of a planar structure follows written conventions (listed elements; open and closed position types; open classes as ALL-CAPS labels, optionally with braces), checked with warnings rather than refusals.

The separate aspiration class is retired and folded into the segmental class as two constructions: aspiration (prominence), prosodically conditioned, and aspiration (fusion), the Yukuna-type segmental pattern.

An intonational class is added: a position belongs to the domain when the intonational pattern applies there (one criterion). Its span rule is auto-derived and awaits review.

Free occurrence has its own sheet. The free/bound answer comes from noninterruption; only bound elements are asked the new columns (left and right edge of a free form, dependent-on-left, dependent-on-right), others get na. It yields a minimal span (the keystone, plus what it depends on if bound) and a maximal one.

Whether the keystone takes part in an analysis is declared per class, overridable per construction: morphosyntactic classes default to not (keystone coded na), phonological blocked-span classes (metrical, segmental) default to yes.
The criterion stressed is renamed accented in the metrical and segmental classes, so it is neutral between stress, pitch accent and other kinds of accent.
No separate decision: na for the keystone is covered by #104; na for other elements waits for a concrete case.

Nonpermutability is coded in two stages: each element is first marked scopal y, n or both (n removes it), then only the remaining pairs of variably ordered elements are coded. Strict non-permutability comes from the planar structure; flexible spans have minimal and maximal forms.
The segmental criterion is named aspirated (was applies), as Adam proposed; obligatoriness is not coded separately on the aspiration sheet.

The English elements coded scopal n at some positions (the modals and AD-S) are scopal both at all their positions; the n values were a coding mistake.

The reflexivization sheet asks whether an element at one position can control a reflexive at another, shown with each position and a direction (forward/backward) rather than every pairing of elements; parallel sheets cover ordinary pronouns and full NPs, to test Principles A, B and C without assuming them.
Superseded by #58: suppletive forms such as went are coded as allomorphy, not as n on the biunique criterion (decided on #238).
English flapping is a construction in the segmental class with one criterion (flapped), coded across position boundaries; there is no separate within-position diagnostic.
Whether an element's scopal value can differ by position is left open: it is treated as a property of the element, and a difference by position is flagged as a question when a language shows one.
English subject and object pronouns are listed one by one in v:npsubj1 and v:obj-part (replacing the PRON class), with no new positions and one you for singular and plural.

Biuniqueness deviations are scoped by Tallman & Auderset's (2023) four categories: coded for English now, built so the other subtypes can be added. English allomorphy (including suppletion) goes through #58. The rest of the thread moved to #263.
